title: After a divided vote
question: Did agreements that passed over a no vote go on to be increased more often than those that passed without one?
finding: The files are too few to say. 20 agreement files that passed over at least one no sit in the chains of linked Board files; 5 of them (25.0%) were followed by a later file that raised the amount. Of 1,125 that passed with no dissent, 211 (18.8%) were. Chance alone would give a gap that wide about 56% of the time, so no difference can be claimed either way. The 5 divided files with a later increase belong to 3 organizations: Mid-Market Foundation; San Francisco Pretrial Diversion Project; TEGSCO, LLC.
how: The Board’s contract, grant and lease files were earlier linked into chains: an agreement and the later files that amend it, joined by contract number, by a cited resolution or by matching amounts (“firm”), or by the same party, department and programme wording (“loose”). For each file in a chain that passed at its final vote, the screen asks whether a later file in the same chain, introduced after that vote, raised the amount. Accepted grants and settlements are not chained and are left out. The rows are the files that passed over a no.
limits: The page on agreements that grew past their first ceiling measures growth per agreement, first ceiling against latest; this screen counts per file and is not comparable with it. An increase is a decision the Board itself voted, not a breach. A loose link can join two different agreements with the same organization. Files passed in the last year or two have had little time to be amended. A no vote does not predict anything here, and with so few divided files it could not be shown if it did. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
